profile: Experimental GCC 17 with 18 locked local patches (source18), C/C++, wasm32-wasi-preview1, static single-threaded linking and freshly rebuilt GNU libstdc++.
sourceLabelBoundary: source17/source18 and diagnostic compiler labels gcc17/gcc18 mean 17/18 locked local patches, not GCC major versions.

dependency.purpose: Strong aliases and patched WABT; generic same-unit weakref optimization can retain local aliases.

patches.purpose: Use VOID_TYPE_P for typedef void returns and indirect function signatures.
Match actual host widths in labels, i64 constants, relocation addends, sizes and memory offsets.
Add opt-in SIMD128 machine modes and GCC RTL instruction patterns; disabled by default.
Match Basic C ABI singleton/empty aggregate arguments/results and narrow scalar extension.
Emit the five-argument external libatomic compare-exchange ABI without changing the builtin declaration.
Add SIMD scalar-count shifts, signed/unsigned and IEEE comparisons, conditional selection and fixed constant shuffles.
Use direct v128 values for enabled vectors and singleton aggregates; preserve vector register modes and aggregate storage.
Implement IEEE binary128 long double storage, soft-float operations and WASI two-i64 argument/indirect-result ABI independently of SIMD.
Enable signed/unsigned int128, WASI paired arguments/indirect results, scalar bitwise complement and SI runtime shift counts.
Ignore ABI-empty C++ records consistently during layout and generic O0 parameter setup without reading absent incoming data.
Use declared type alignment/storage units for named bitfields and classify singleton ABI values with the original declared storage type; preserve packed and unnamed-field rules.
Ignore unnamed bitfields when classifying singleton ABI values, preserve raw storage offsets, and retain empty aggregate storage modes without emitting an unused hard return local.
Add signed/unsigned i8x16 and i16x8 saturating add/subtract optabs and typed GCC target builtins with explicit SIMD feature gating.
Expose GNU __float128, exact Q/q literal typing, distinct C++ mangling, consistent same-format conversion ranks and GNU library feature detection over the qualified binary128 representation.
Add baseline SIMD conversion optabs and exactly typed saturation builtins, with composed packs/high halves and existing scalar fallbacks.
Install the documented 169-name SIMD128 header, typed direct lane operations and scalar/vector partial-copy legalization without changing the public vector ABI.
Define strong function/data aliases with shared addresses and independent symbol binding, visibility and relocations.
Normalize optional weak reference imports and asm-labelled symbol references, with typed weak target collection and strong-reference precedence.
Record actual SIMD instructions and v128 types, merge target_features and reject malformed or conflicting declarations.
Resolve strong symbol aliases and preserve independent linking names and relocation identities through annotated WAT and binary round trips.

coverage: Initialized pointers, local addresses and direct calls
Absent optional definitions and GCC/Clang providers
Weak definitions and strong overrides in both object orders
Direct strong use before/after weakref use
Merely declared targets, unused refs and multiple weakrefs
Explicit assembler names and C++ overloaded i32/f64 targets
Fresh GNU vector/string/I/O consumers with both provider families

objectContract.targets: Exact linking-v2 names, function/data kinds, weak/global binding, definition status, compiler-specific visibility and function signatures.
objectContract.externalWeakrefs: Local declaration alias names, including C++ local mangling and explicit assembler names, must not survive as linking symbols.
objectContract.relocations: Actual target/alias-selected relocations are preserved in receipts. Initialized function/data pointers require types 2/5; local pointer sites require types 1/4; direct-call profiles also require type 0.

definedTargetAliases.required: Local, defined, default visibility; same function entity index or exact data segment/offset/size; no forwarding body or copied storage.
definedTargetAliases.clang: Direct target references with no local alias symbols.
definedTargetAliases.genericSource: gcc/ipa-visibility.cc optimize_weakref, locally bound same-unit definitions only.

objectContract.visibility: Clang definitions are hidden by default; GCC definitions use default visibility. Binding is checked independently.

gnuRuntime.boundary: GNU libraries were freshly rebuilt with source18. The SDK33 libc/CRT/libm/builtins bytes were preserved; they are not claimed to be rebuilt from GCC source.

inheritedRegression.countingBoundary: Inherited case rows include assembler checks and other suite-specific units; this total is not a count of WASI program executions. Weakref480/48 counts remain separate.

sameTranslationUnit.identityBoundary: Each GCC build preserves alias-to-target body/storage identity within every object. The two compiler builds do not need to emit byte-identical objects.
sameTranslationUnit.runtimeBoundary: Fresh source18 work libc used for all three compiler controls.

hostGcc.boundary: Host ELF control of generic local .set aliases. Native ELF C++ local data name can be mangled; not counted as Wasm qualification.

smallNative18Probe.boundary: Compatibility probe used preserved source17 libc. It is separate from the same-source GNU/native-v2 qualification.

offlineObjectReview.boundary: Reinspection of original v1 objects with corrected defined-target rules; does not substitute for final recompilation and execution.

causes: The initial inspector incorrectly forbade GCC generic same-unit local aliases in eight definition consumers.
URI-escaped %3A output directory names caused wasm-ld output creation to fail; an identical link using a safe path passed.
preservedInitialAttempt.resolution: Only the known defined-target local aliases are allowed, with shared body/storage checks. Filesystem names use a verified collision-free alphabet. The entire matrix was recompiled and rerun in native-v2 without changing compiler, assembler or GNU runtime inputs.

boundaries: Weak alias definitions remain rejected; ordinary weak definitions and external weak references are qualified.
COMDAT groups, symbol versioning, shared/dynamic linking, threads/TLS, exceptions and RTTI remain outside this contract.
Mixed GCC/Clang cases establish only the recorded signatures/layouts, not general C++ ABI or runtime compatibility.

browser.boundary: GCC-only public SDK executions, object metadata, raw mixed-object link controls and actual Chromium Worker/Node checks are separate from completed native qualification. Browser/Worker evidence will be added after those jobs finish.
